result.text: Daridorexant 25 mg met WASO (12-minute improvement vs placebo at Month 1 and 10-minute improvement at Month 3) but did not reject the null for LPS (LPS 25 mg treatment effect -6.45 min at Month 1, p=0.0302, and -9.01 min at Month 3, p=0.0052, not meeting threshold); 10 mg not superior to placebo on any endpoint

citations.quote: The 25-mg dose showed a 12-minute improvement compared to placebo at Month 1 and a 10-minute improvement at Month 3, while treatment response was unchanged from Month 1 to Month 3.
The 10-mg daridorexant dose arm did not demonstrate superiority to placebo on any endpoint and will therefore not be discussed further.

target_moa.text: Daridorexant is a dual orexin receptor antagonist (DORA); its mechanism in insomnia is thought to be through antagonism of orexin 1 (OX1R) and orexin 2 (OX2R) receptors, blocking wake-promoting orexin neuropeptide signaling (Ki = 0.47 and 0.93 nM, respectively)

citations.quote: The mechanism of action of daridorexant in the treatment of insomnia is unknown but thought to be through antagonism of orexin 1 (OX1R) and 2 (OX2R) receptors. The orexin neuropeptide signaling system plays a role in wakefulness.
Daridorexant binds to and inhibits orexin receptors, OX1R and OX2R (Ki = 0.47 and 0.93nM, respectively).
